description: We are Team Schwarzchildren from Bangladesh
summary:
ORBIT-LENS is an interactive, multi-epoch infrared sky explorer and time-series blink comparator engineered to uncover high-proper-motion objects—including brown dwarfs, Kuiper Belt objects, and hypothetical Planet X candidates—across SPHEREx observation epochs.

Powered by an Astropy/NumPy scientific engine and a hardware-accelerated WebGL2/Three.js interface, ORBIT-LENS unifies multi-band infrared imagery across SPHEREx’s 6 detector arrays (0.75–5.00 μm, 102 spectral channels). It directly solves the challenge by transforming petabyte-scale all-sky surveys into intuitive discovery workflows: an interactive difference blinker, volumetric 3D Time-Cubes, real-time Spectral Energy Distribution (SED) profiling, and multi-wavelength cross-matching against live AllWISE, 2MASS, and Gaia DR3 TAP catalogs. Built-in WCAG 2.2 AA photosafety controls enforce safe flicker rates (capped at 3.0 Hz), complemented by Web Audio sonification for accessible, multimodal data perception.

ORBIT-LENS bridges rigorous astrometric calibration with modern, responsive visual analytics—empowering astrophysicists and citizen scientists alike to rapidly validate faint moving targets, classify variable phenomena, and map the unexplored frontiers of our solar system.
details:
ORBIT-LENS is an interactive multi-epoch infrared sky observatory and time-series blink comparator designed to discover high-proper-motion celestial bodies—such as outer Solar System asteroids, Kuiper Belt objects, brown dwarfs, and hypothetical Planet X candidates—as well as infrared variable stars across SPHEREx observation epochs.

The system operates across a two-tier architecture:

  1. Astrometric & Scientific Engine (Python Backend): Astropy and NumPy maintain absolute authority over all celestial mathematics, handling WCS-TAN (World Coordinate System Gnomonic) projections, FITS Level 2 MEF (Multi-Extension FITS) parsing across HDU 1 (Science), HDU 2 (Variance), and HDU 3 (Bitmask), and pixel-by-pixel SNR calculations. It queries live TAP (Table Access Protocol) and SIA v2 services from NASA/IPAC IRSA, CDS Strasbourg, and ESA Gaia DR3, backed by an offline simulation engine with zero silent fallbacks.
  2. GPU-Accelerated Client (WebGL2 / Three.js Frontend): The client provides instant, interactive visual exploration through four synchronized viewports:
    • All-Sky Interactive Map: 2D canvas with full Pan-and-Zoom, 1:1 astrometric cursor tracking, and celestial grid overlays.
    • Difference Blinker: Hardware-accelerated subtraction engine blinking temporal epochs with adjustable stretch curves (Linear, Asinh, Square Root, Logarithmic) and 8 scientific colormaps (Viridis, Inferno, Magma, Plasma, Greyscale, Coolwarm, Cividis, Spectral).
    • Volumetric 3D Time-Cube: Temporal and spectral raymarching projecting multi-epoch slices into an explorable 3D volume.
    • Spectral Energy Distribution (SED) Drawer: Real-time flux profiling across all 6 physical SPHEREx detector arrays (0.75–5.00 μm, 102 continuous channels).

What Benefits Does It Have?

  • Accelerated Discovery: Blinks epochs and generates difference frames in milliseconds on client GPUs, reducing hours of manual FITS analysis into seconds.
  • Cross-Survey Verification: Instantly cross-identifies SPHEREx infrared detections against high-resolution archival surveys (AllWISE W1/W2, 2MASS J/H/Ks, and ESA Gaia DR3 astrometry).
  • Quality & Artifact Rejection: Visualizes raw bitmask quality flags (cosmic rays, saturation, bad pixels) side-by-side with science frames, preventing false-positive discoveries.
  • Multimodal Accessibility: Transforms spectral curves into musical pitches using Web Audio sonification, enabling researchers and visually impaired astronomers to hear infrared absorption features (e.g., 1.66 μm CH41.66\,\mu\text{m}\ \text{CH}_41.66μm CH4​, 3.05 μm H2O3.05\,\mu\text{m}\ \text{H}_2\text{O}3.05μm H2​O ice, 4.27 μm CO24.27\,\mu\text{m}\ \text{CO}_24.27μm CO2​).

Intended Impact

ORBIT-LENS democratizes time-domain infrared astrophysics. By bridging automated NASA archival pipelines with an intuitive, zero-install web interface, it turns complex multi-spectral datasets into actionable discoveries. It serves professional astrophysicists conducting target verification, university classrooms studying stellar evolution and astrometry, and citizen scientists hunting for unknown Solar System objects in SPHEREx's cosmic survey legacy.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software

  • Languages: Python 3.12 (Backend), TypeScript / ES2022 (Frontend), GLSL (WebGL2 Shaders).
  • Backend Framework & Libraries: FastAPI, Uvicorn, Astropy (WCS, FITS I/O), NumPy, PyVO (TAP / SIA queries), HTTPX (async networking).
  • Frontend Framework & Rendering: React 19, Vite, Three.js / React Three Fiber (3D Time-Cube), WebGL2 Custom Shaders, Tailwind CSS, Lucide Icons, uPlot (microsecond SED charting).
  • State Management & Audio: Zustand v5 (with URL deep-link synchronization), Web Audio API (synthesizer sonification).
  • Deployment & Testing: Vercel (Frontend & Edge Routing), Render (Python ASGI Web Service), Pytest, Vitest.

Creative Highlights

  • Volumetric Time-Cube: Transforms static 2D astronomical cutouts into an interactive 3D spatial/temporal continuum where motion appears as tilted trajectories through spacetime.
  • Accessible Sonification: Spectral fluxes are translated into pitch frequencies via logarithmic frequency mapping, making infrared spectral signatures audible.
  • Modern Glassmorphic UI: Eliminates 1990s desktop astronomical clutter in favor of a sleek, distraction-free cockpit featuring collapsible HUD drawers, unified coordinate transforms, and responsive viewport splitters.

Critical Factors Considered by Our Team

  1. WCAG 2.2 AA Photosafety: Rapid blinking in time-series software can trigger photo-sensitive epileptic responses. We hard-capped blinking at 3.0 Hz (defaulting to a calm 0.5 fps), strictly initialized playback in a paused state, and implemented smooth trackpad/wheel scrubbing for user-controlled epoch stepping.
  2. Scientific Data Integrity: Client-side rendering never modifies underlying scientific pixel values. Color mapping, stretching, and differencing are executed entirely in GPU fragment shaders while raw astronomical computations remain strictly on the Astropy backend.
  3. Data Source Transparency: The application explicitly labels data origins at all times with dynamic status badges (SPHEREx QR3, SYNTHETIC, MAST, VizieR) to prevent synthetic or cached data from being mistaken for live telescope telemetry.
  4. Reproducibility & Deep Linking: Every view state—including celestial coordinates (α,δ\alpha, \deltaα,δ), Field of View, active spectral band, epoch index, and overlay choice—is continuously serialized into URL search parameters for one-click collaborative sharing.
